## Why this course?

Fitting a mechanistic model to data is a common task in an research on infectious disease dynamics.

::: {.fragment}
The methods are often buried in the statistical literature, with little guidance on which particularapproach one should use.
:::

::: {.fragment}
There was no single place that taught them together.
:::

## The history

Taught at LSHTM for over a decade, by the Centre for the Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Diseases.

::: {.fragment}
Written by Anton Camacho and Sebastian Funk, and developed since by [several people](../../authors.qmd).
:::

::: {.fragment}
It used R and a course-only package, which we told people never to use for real work.
:::

::: {.fragment}
This year it is **Julia** (bear with us), which can express every method we teach.
:::

## Who are you?

Around the room:

- your name
- where you have come from
- what you would like to fit a model to

## How the course works

Each session opens with a short set of slides and then becomes a practical you work through.

::: {.fragment}
The practicals are the course. Sit with someone and compare answers, and ask us as soon as you are stuck.
:::

::: {.fragment}
Every line of Julia is given complete. The exercises ask you to predict, interpret and choose, never to debug.
:::
